answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards as a digital kernel for identity, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must wander across 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct content. Like a shepherd searching a knoll for lost sheep, the verifier requests random shards at every epoch. Any failure to return segments triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash to prevent collusion, ensuring the honest agent cost stays low while farm overhead scales linearly, preventing sybil exploitation.
